title: Divided votes on money files where the counterparty was in a voting member’s donor circle
question: On which divided Board votes on a contract, grant, lease or settlement was the named counterparty already in the donor circle of a member who voted, and how did that member vote?
finding: Of 123 divided final Board votes on money files from 2015 to 2026, 45 name an outside organization as counterparty, and on 7 of those the organization was already in the donor circle of at least one member who voted: 14 member-and-vote pairs in all, 11 ayes and 3 noes. Every link is money from donors who named the organization as their employer; the largest link is $950. The set is too small to test on its own; the comparison with members outside the donor circle is in the screen “Divided votes: with a donor’s side, and with everyone else’s”.
how: Two public records are set side by side. From the Board’s roll calls: the final Board passage roll call of each money file (as the shared roll-call reader defines it) that had at least one aye and one no and whose title names an outside organization; grants the City accepts, public bodies and private individuals are left out. From the campaign-finance filings: money given before the day of the vote to a voting member’s candidate committees, to a ballot committee carrying the member’s name or to a committee others formed to support the member, by the organization in its own name or by donors who wrote it as their employer. Each row is one roll call and one counterparty; the member column gives every voting member with such a link, the vote printed for that member, the kind of link, its amount up to the vote and the date of the first contribution. A link in which everything given had been returned before the vote is not counted. The file link opens the Clerk’s vote page for that roll call, or the published minutes where the roll call was read from them. The title, the counterparty and the dollar amount of every row in this list were read against the file’s full title; a note says where the machine-read value was corrected.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt, and a link is not a reason for a vote. Nearly every member votes for nearly every money file, whoever the counterparty is: these roll calls passed with most of the unconnected members voting aye as well (see the last column). A donor who names an employer says where that donor works; it does not show that the employer gave or asked for anything, and at a large employer it says very little. Donors give to members who already share their view. The amounts are small beside the contracts. Only divided roll calls are listed, because a unanimous vote says nothing about one member. Names are matched exactly, so some links are missed. Individual donors are counted, never named. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
